messages:
maria_ops: Heads-up — capacity forecast for us-west shows hosted API demand outpacing our committed GPU minutes for the next 3 weekly buckets. shortfall ~8-15% depending on burst patterns. pinging infra + finance :eyes:

sam_enginfra: grim but expected after the new customer onboarded. do we have the per-queue breakdown? esp. small-gen vs. embed traffic.

lee_sre: I pulled node-level metrics. Most of the pressure is on g4dn-like pools (low-memory types) during 12:00-18:00 PT. Spike cadence matches batch embed jobs + retries.

jordan_fin: Cost note — if we exceed committed minutes we get charged premium on spot/burst pricing. current estimate: ~$14k incremental this month if we absorb all excess. we can do a short-term top-up commitment but it has a 30d billing impact.

maria_ops: quick data: capacity-bot reports: week1 demand 415k reserved-equivalent minutes, committed 385k -> shortfall 7.8%; week2 demand 460k vs committed 390k -> 17.9%; week3 420k vs 400k -> 5%. detailed CSV linked: https://redwood.internal/reports/2432109876-capa.csv

sam_enginfra: options: 1) temporary reserved bump (30d) to cover week2 spike 2) move low-priority embed jobs to off-peak via scheduling policy 3) enable preemptible fallback + throttling 4) accept premium cloud billing and monitor. Which combo is acceptable?

lee_sre: I'd prioritize job-scheduling first. we can shift some customer batch embeds to a delayed queue with backoff. config snippet to test: ```yaml
queue: embed-delayed
max_workers: 40
window: 02:00-06:00 PT
```

capacity-bot: automated calc: short-term reserved bump (30d) to cover wk2 => +40k minutes => estimated cost delta $9,600; projected avoided burst spend if we don't throttle ~$16,000. ROI looks positive for wk2 only.

jordan_fin: If we commit, let's do a targeted SKU-level reserve to avoid long-term exposure. finance prefers 30d or 60d flexible rather than annual. Also need signoff on the contract amendment.

maria_ops: tradeoffs: bump reserves avoids customer latency regressions but increases committed line item; scheduling reduces cost but may increase latency for some customers. need decision by EOD to lock procurement timelines for a 30d reserve.

sam_enginfra: quick runbook: (1) immediately flag heavy embed jobs and add to delayed queue (2) enable 10% request shedding on non-critical routes (config PR incoming) (3) if after 6 hours shortfall persists, trigger reserved bump. I'll open a PR for the shedding rule.

lee_sre: also found a misconfigured autoscaler in us-west that wasn't respecting max_nodes=120 for the g4 pool; fixing that reduces shortfall by ~6k minutes/hour when traffic is steady. fix rolling out now.

jordan_fin: I'll hold off on procurement until we see post-fix numbers. If the autoscaler + scheduling knocks down the projection under 10% we can avoid the bump. finance will pre-approve up to $12k emergency spend if can't be avoided.

maria_ops: agreed. action items: sam -> PR for shedding + scheduling, lee -> autoscaler fix deploy (monitor 3h), capacity-bot -> re-run forecast every 30m and post updates here. i'll coordinate procurement if we still need the reserve. :thumbsup:

capacity-bot: next forecast update scheduled at 2432110176 (in ~16m). current expected shortfall after autoscaler fix: down to 5-12% across windows.

sam_enginfra: thanks — looping in @product-ops to communicate potential degraded embed freshness.

maria_ops: closing loop later with final decision. cheers.
